name: mannequin.js
notes: 2026-11-01: Procedural jointed human figure on Three.js; poses are joint angles, so a pose can be a pure function of t. Proposed route: render through the three-js capture path.
2026-11-01: Captured from conversation; listed-in-prd is the schema's listed-only status. Licence, version and maintenance not yet assessed.
2026-11-01: Triage: assess. Concrete job: human figures and character motion, absent from the catalogue.

2026-11-24: Guide written from partial evidence (mannequin-js-pose-capture): figure units about 1 per figure height; GPL-3.0 flagged for redistribution.

evidence.result: partial: 90 frames 1280x720, shuffled equals sequential; joint readbacks (torso bend, right arm raise, left knee bend) match the values set from t; four predeclared frames distinct; knee-only change smaller than torso-and-arm change; corner alpha 0. Failed predeclared check: right wrist moved 0.404 library units t=0 to 1.5 s vs 1.0 required (figure 1.01 units tall). Reruns byte-identical. three 0.186.1, Chromium 156.0.8078.4, Node v22.19.0
evidence.scope: Fixture-reported: joints posed from t, frames deterministic and distinct, alpha ok; wrist displacement check failed (0.40 vs 1.0 units); macOS arm64

source: conversation 2026-11-01: character and figure tooling gap
summary: Three.js procedural articulated human figures with joint-angle posing, suited to simple pose-driven scenes without importing a character asset.
use_when: When a lightweight posed human figure is enough
When pose values can be generated directly in a Three.js scene
avoid_when: When you need realistic custom characters or rigging: mpfb
When you need VRM avatars: three-vrm

assessment.rationale: Upstream describes a simple articulated human figure and latest release v5.2.3 (2026-10-06), upgraded to Three.js r169; the repository license is GPL-3. Keep as a lightweight procedural figure option, with the copyleft license visible in the card.
